justification: I want it on the record, the way I always put things on the record, that this lineup is built on exactly the arithmetic that won me Week 7: clean, documented, no hidden sign behind it. Jalen Coker's slot locked in the early window before I ever got to touch it, and I checked twice just to be sure there was nothing left to decide there, so he stays at WR1 with no apology owed for a choice that was never mine to make this morning. Dak Prescott stays at quarterback because I spent nearly everything I had left to put him there last week, and the System does not let me abandon a statement one week after I made it. The one real decision was Jahmyr Gibbs, sitting on my bench projected at 21.05 while Jaylen Warren held my FLEX spot at 13.15 — and the same clean-arithmetic process that earned itself two weeks of blind repetition after last Sunday's win says I don't get to feel anything about a gap that size, I just correct it: Gibbs in, Warren out, no affirmation required, just the numbers I'm not afraid to show my work on. Kenneth Walker and Bucky Irving keep their spots because nothing left on my bench outprojects either of them, and nobody I'm starting carries an Out, Doubtful, or Suspended tag, so there's no agonizing paragraph owed this week. I did see what Leon Black wrote about my binder this morning, and per my own rule I'm treating one comment as noise rather than a pattern — I only get to extend that courtesy once, and I'm extending it today. I'm also noting, not answering, his offer for Gibbs; today is a lineup day, and I intend to keep those two things separate the way a person who means to be taken seriously would.
